title: Triage 100+ Customer Support Emails Overnight & Draft Empathetic Replies
oneLiner: Automatically classify incoming tickets by urgency, draft accurate troubleshooting steps from your help docs, and queue them for morning one-click approval.
problem: Solo founders and small support teams wake up to an overflowing inbox of 80+ customer questions every Monday morning. Most are repetitive inquiries (order tracking, refund policies, password resets) mixed with 2-3 genuine urgent emergencies.
workflow: Connected the agent to the incoming support inbox with read and draft permissions (never send directly).
Gave the agent the official knowledge base and FAQs markdown file.
Every night, the agent labeled incoming tickets (Urgent, Billing, How-To, Bug) and prepared drafted responses for human review at 8 AM.
prompt:
You are a thoughtful, world-class customer support specialist for [COMPANY NAME].

Reference our knowledge base below:
[PASTE FAQ / KNOWLEDGE BASE SUMMARY HERE]

Read the incoming customer message:
"[PASTE CUSTOMER TICKET HERE]"

Provide:
1. Ticket Urgency Tag: [P1 Urgent / P2 Moderate / P3 Routine]
2. Category Tag: [Bug / Billing / Shipping / Feedback / Question]
3. Sentiment Assessment: [Delighted / Neutral / Frustrated / Angry]
4. Draft Response: Written in a warm, polite, and reassuring tone. Cite exact policy steps. Do not apologize unnecessarily if no fault occurred; focus on immediate resolution.
5. Escalation Flag: Does this require human manager approval? (Yes / No and why).

realityCheck.firstTryMistake: The agent was initially too eager to offer refunds outside company policy until strict discount/refund guidelines were hard-coded in the prompt.
realityCheck.manualCleanupTime: Roughly 30 seconds per ticket to review and click 'Send' in the morning.
realityCheck.limitations: Never allow an AI to auto-send replies directly to angry or billing-dispute customers without human eye-balls.
